title: Whether the read-time gate survives a corpus the hypothesis was not formed on

verdicts.registered: the run is measurable: every question evaluated once, gold executable, no leaks
the full arm is not positive, and not significantly different from the none arm
the read-time gate is worth between +0.2pp and +2.0pp on train
the gate shrinks and by less than half: a point estimate in [0.49, 0.98]
an imported identifier is still a negative covariate

statement: Out of sample, memory costs 0.71pp. The read-time gate recovers 0.51pp of it, leaving -0.20pp, which is not distinguishable from no memory.
notes: The clustered interval is the one that decides this round. Questions inside a database are not independent — one package of rules reaches all of them — so the interval resamples databases. The question-level interval is in the source artefact and is narrower on train by 0.03pp, which is why it was not the one quoted.
No accuracy is compared across the two splits. Dev and train share no database, so only the paired differences between arms are the same quantity.
The dev column of the table is the reading this round was registered against. It is recomputed here rather than quoted from the documentation, so the two cannot drift.
